items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: Buck Clayton, my old friend and mentor was willing to help me out and he played the trumpet.

ctx.x: And that's where I really got introduced to jazz formally by Wilbur, W-i-l-b-u-r, known as Buck, B-u-c-k, last name Clayton, C-l-a-y-t-o-n.
Now, Sir Charles, what did Buck mean to you, where did you meet him, and what came off that meeting?

items.title: 67246_Buck Clayton oral history interview
items.q: In my house was all of the young, aspiring, young musicians wanted to meet me, Sir Charles was one.

ctx.x: He was born I believe on the same street that I was born on in Kansas, Parsons, called Grand Avenue. In fact, he was born about three blocks from me, but he was just one of three or four brothers at that time. I didn't know anything about him playing music until I came back from Shang Hai, China and I went home to visit my mother. And in my house was all of the young, aspiring, young musicians wanted to meet me, Sir Charles was one.
